assumptions: Fidelity is the measured T4 ligase data the scorer uses.
limits: A greedy-plus-steepest-ascent search: no claim of finding the optimum.
The golden grades the fidelity objective, not the search path.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which overhang set of a given size ligates with high fidelity by measured data, keeping any junctions that cannot change?

description: Design a high-fidelity Golden Gate overhang set of a given size against measured ligation data, optionally pinning junctions you cannot change (a fixed vector's own overhangs). The counterpart to score_overhang_fidelity: that grades a set you already have, this proposes one. The search is greedy-plus-steepest-ascent over the same golden-validated objective: real measured data, a heuristic path, no claim of finding the optimum.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

candidate_pool.description: how many of the strongest-annealing overhangs the search considers. Higher is a better set and a slower run. Advanced.

dataset.description: design against this measured matrix instead of the one the enzyme implies. Values: BsaI-HFv2 (BsaI-HFv2, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), BsmBI-v2 (BsmBI-v2, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), Esp3I (Esp3I, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), BbsI-HF (BbsI-HF, Golden Gate cycling (4 nt)), SapI (SapI, Golden Gate cycling (3 nt)), T4-01h-25C (T4 DNA ligase, 1 h at 25 C (4 nt)), T4-01h-37C (T4 DNA ligase, 1 h at 37 C (4 nt)), T4-18h-25C (T4 DNA ligase, 18 h at 25 C (4 nt)), T4-18h-37C (T4 DNA ligase, 18 h at 37 C (4 nt)).

enzyme.description: the Type-IIS enzyme the reaction uses, which picks that enzyme's own measured matrix when one exists. Only applies when dataset is not given.

fixed.description: junctions you cannot change, such as a destination vector's own overhangs. They are never considered for replacement and are counted inside `size`.

size.description: how many junctions the assembly needs (parts + 1 for a circular construct, counted as junctions).

start_from.description: the set you already have, as a second starting point. Given one of the same size, the answer is never WORSE than it: the greedy build alone can land in its own basin and lose points against a real set. Wire `golden_gate_assemble.overhangs` here.

name: design_overhang_set

fidelity.description: the designed set's fidelity, 0-1, on the same measured matrix

fixed.description: the junctions that were pinned and never replaced

from.description: which starting point won: `greedy` for the built set, `yours` for `start_from` improved in place

overhangs.description: the designed set, pinned junctions first. Wire it into score_overhang_fidelity to see the full per-junction breakdown

percent.description: the same number as a percentage
